item.title: No media ban | Bure’ clarifies ministry’s position
item.description: THERE is no media ban on schools competing in the Vodafone Super Deans Championship, the Ministry of Education has clarified. Deputy Secretary for Primary and Secondary Education Timoci Bure clarified that schools were free to speak to the media about their rugby teams — but not during official teaching and learning hours.
item.content:encoded:
THERE is no media ban on schools competing in the Vodafone Super Deans Championship, the Ministry of Education has clarified.

Deputy Secretary for Primary and Secondary Education Timoci Bure clarified that schools were free to speak to the media about their rugby teams — but not during official teaching and learning hours.

Bure said the ministry’s policy had been misunderstood by schools, resulting in media organisations being told they needed ministry approval before interviewing teams and school officials.

He said the restriction applied only to official working hours.

Primary schools operate from 8am to 2.30pm, while secondary schools operate from 8am to 3.30pm. Outside those hours, schools can speak directly to the media about their sporting teams without seeking approval from the ministry.

“They can attend the interview any time after working hours. That is a sports team. They should explain everything about their sports team,” Bure said.

The clarification comes as the Super Deans Championship enters its decisive stage, with schools across the country preparing for the biggest matches of the season.

Bure said the ministry had no reason to control information about individual school teams.

“The school team — nobody knows anything about the school team. Only them.”

He said the only matters schools could not comment on were Ministry of Education decisions, policies or directives. T

hose questions must be referred to the ministry.

But team selections, preparations, performances and other matters concerning a school’s sporting program can be discussed directly with the media.

The clarification follows concerns raised by media organisations after several schools said interviews and visits had to be vetted by the ministry.

Bure said that was a misunderstanding of the policy and indicated the ministry would address the issue with schools.

For the hundreds of students involved in the Super Deans Championship — and the schools using the competition to showcase their young talent — the message is clear: The ministry has not shut the door on the media.

item.title: Support grows for Ra High
item.description: Ra is united. The province is riding a wave of rugby success, and Ra High School is now at the centre of it. After helping Ra create history by winning the Vodafone Vanua Challenge and earning promotion to the Skipper Cup next season, the schoolboys have given the province another reason to celebrate.
item.content:encoded:
Ra is united. The province is riding a wave of rugby success, and Ra High School is now at the centre of it.

After helping Ra create history by winning the Vodafone Vanua Challenge and earning promotion to the Skipper Cup next season, the schoolboys have given the province another reason to celebrate.

Ra High stunned defending champions Ratu Kadavulevu School 12-10 in last week’s Vodafone Super Deans Under-18 quarter-final to reach the semi-finals for the first time.

They now face Southern Zone champions Suva Grammar School at Churchill Park in Lautoka this weekend.

But for Ra, the semi-final is bigger than a school rugby match. It has become a rallying point for an entire province.

Ra Rugby Union has called off all its provincial club matches this weekend to allow players and supporters to travel to Lautoka and get behind the schoolboys.

Ratu Josaia Niudamu, Assistant Minister for Justice and a chief from the vanua of Nalawa, said the achievement had brought the people of Ra together.

He said the support for the school had grown significantly, with Ra people from across Fiji and overseas now getting behind the team.

“The supporters that we have never seen in the past years, now we have seen the number of supporters growing. Not only from within the province of Ra, but the whole of Fiji and also those overseas.”

The victory over RKS has been particularly significant.

“It is a surprise to me and also to the people of Ra that we have managed to defeat the defending champion RKS last week and now we have gone on to the semis,” he said.

The excitement comes at a time when Ra rugby is enjoying one of its biggest breakthroughs. The province recently won the Vodafone Vanua Challenge, securing promotion to the Skipper Cup — Fiji’s premier provincial competition — next season.

Niudamu said the school had received support from Ra people living in towns and cities, those overseas, Fiji Water and other stakeholders.

But this weekend, he wants the entire vanua at Churchill Park.

“We are all going down to Churchill Park to rally behind our boys.”

For Ra High, the challenge is now clear. Beat Suva Grammar and the school will reach the Vodafone Super Deans final for the first time.

For Ra, it would be another milestone in a season that has already changed the province’s rugby fortunes. Ra High is now chasing a place in the Deans final. And the people of Ra are ready to follow.

item.title: Trust backs netball academy’s NZ tour
item.description: THE under-15 Royale Rising Star team from the Nakoivalu Netball Academy has received a financial boost ahead of its international campaign in Christchurch, New Zealand later this month. The Fijian Holding Unit Trust handed over cash sponsorship to the team today and also opened an investment account for the young netballers as they prepare to compete at the International Netball Festival from Augu
item.content:encoded:
THE under-15 Royale Rising Star team from the Nakoivalu Netball Academy has received a financial boost ahead of its international campaign in Christchurch, New Zealand later this month.

The Fijian Holding Unit Trust handed over cash sponsorship to the team today and also opened an investment account for the young netballers as they prepare to compete at the International Netball Festival from August 26-28.

The team comprises of students from Suva Grammar School, Mahatma Ghandi Memorial High School, Adi Cakobau School, St Joseph Secondary School and The Learning Centre School and Veiuto Primary School.

Speaking during the hand over event, Academy founder Unaisi Ranavue said the Christchurch trip was initially planned as a self-funded tour, with players who could fund their own travel given the first opportunity to be part of the squad.

“First options were given to those that can self-fund their trip,” Ranavue said.

The tournament will be the team’s first appearance at the festival, which celebrates its 50th Anniversary.

Parents and team executive then worked to raise funds and approach potential sponsors to support the tour.

The team has completed its strength and conditioning and core preparations and is now focused on court work ahead of the tournament.

The three-day festival will feature pool matches, followed by the finals.

For some of the players, the tournament will be their first opportunity to travel overseas and compete internationally.

Ranavue also said the sponsorship and investment account were an important step of supporting the players for their Christchurch campaign and beyond.

She also said the tour represented a major milestone for the players.

“We’ve been hearing about it. But we’ve never been part of it. So, this is a huge milestone for us to be part of the competition.”

item.title: A special win for Ba, Dayal
item.description: SEVEN years after their last league triumph, the Men in Black are back on top and Ba Football Club president Praneel Dayal believes the return to glory is more than just the end of a trophy drought. Ba sealed the Extra Premier League title after a dominant campaign, adding the league crown to the Fiji FACT title they won earlier this season.
item.content:encoded:
SEVEN years after their last league triumph, the Men in Black are back on top and Ba Football Club president Praneel Dayal believes the return to glory is more than just the end of a trophy drought.

Ba sealed the Extra Premier League title after a dominant campaign, adding the league crown to the Fiji FACT title they won earlier this season.

The two major trophies fulfil a target Dayal once described as more than enough under his leadership.

But as the celebrations continue, Dayal says the achievements are not the destination.

They are the foundation of what he hopes will become a new chapter for one of Fiji’s most successful football clubs.

“It is very difficult to put into words what this achievement means to me personally.

“When I took on this responsibility, my objective was never simply to win one trophy. The bigger objective was to rebuild Ba Football Club into a properly structured, professionally managed and competitive football organisation.”

For seven years, the league title had eluded Ba, leaving supporters longing for the days when the black-and-yellow side dominated Fiji football.

Dayal says rebuilding the club required more than simply recruiting better players.

The administration, finances, coaching, player welfare, recruitment, discipline, sponsorship and relationship with supporters all had to be addressed.

“The biggest challenge was understanding that you cannot rebuild a football club by changing only the players. You have to rebuild the entire environment around the team,” he said.

After several seasons without a league title, Dayal believed the club had to change its mindset and restore the expectation that Ba should always be challenging for major honours.

“We needed to change that mentality. We wanted everyone associated with Ba to believe that competing for trophies is not an ambition it is the standard,” he said.

That change in mentality was reflected on the field this season.

Winning the Fiji FACT provided the first major indication that the rebuilding process was beginning to bear fruit.

The league title then followed, proving to Dayal that the success was not simply a one-off tournament triumph.

“Winning the Fiji FACT was a very special moment because it gave everyone the belief that we were moving in the right direction,” he said.

“Winning the Extra Premier League afterwards confirmed that it was not a one-off achievement. It demonstrated that we had built a team capable of performing consistently over an entire season.”

Dayal believes the strength of the current side lies in its combination of talent, coaching, unity and mentality.

While Ba have quality and experienced players capable of changing matches, he says the most important factor has been the willingness of the squad to put the team ahead of individual interests.

“The biggest difference is the combination of talent, coaching, unity and mentality.

“We created a squad where everyone understood that the team comes before the individual.”

The coaching staff, he added, played a major role in bringing different personalities and playing styles together and turning them into one competitive unit.

For Dayal, the consistency shown throughout the league season was particularly impressive.

“What impressed me most was their consistency, discipline and willingness to fight for each other. ”

But while the players and coaches have been the face of Ba’s success, Dayal is quick to acknowledge the work of those operating away from the spotlight.

Board members, team officials, medical personnel, volunteers, sponsors and supporters all played a part in creating the platform for the team to succeed.

“Our players deserve tremendous credit. They have worked hard, sacrificed, accepted competition for places and, most importantly, played for the badge,” he added.

He also paid tribute to generations of Ba players, officials and administrators who built the club’s proud football history.

“We did not create Ba’s football legacy; we inherited it.

item.title: Fiji duo back in black
item.description: FIJIAN-BORN stars Timoci Tavatavanawai and Emoni Narawa are back in black. The pair will make their much-anticipated return to the All Blacks when New Zealand faces the Sharks in South Africa tomorrow.
item.content:encoded:
FIJIAN-BORN stars Timoci Tavatavanawai and Emoni Narawa are back in black.

The pair will make their much-anticipated return to the All Blacks when New Zealand faces the Sharks in South Africa tomorrow.

Their selection in the All Blacks match-day 23 marks the first time either player will take the field for New Zealand on the 2026 Greatest Rivalry tour.

For Tavatavanawai, it is a return more than a year in the making.

The powerful winger last played for the All Blacks in July 2025 when he made his Test debut against France in Wellington.

Narawa’s return comes after a difficult end to his last international outing.

He scored against the Springboks at Eden Park in September last year before being forced off with a rib injury.

Now both Fijian-born players have another opportunity to stake their claim at Test level.

Their return will be closely followed in Fiji, where both players remain popular figures among rugby fans.

Tavatavanawai and Narawa are among a growing group of Fijian-born players making their mark on the international stage.

For the two wingers, Wednesday’s clash is about more than simply returning to the All Blacks.

It is an opportunity to remind New Zealand selectors of what they can offer — and to reignite their Test careers.

item.title: Rugby House set for facelift
item.description: FIJI Rugby is set to restore pride in the home of the national game with a facelift for Rugby House and the High-Performance Unit (HPU) Gym through a new partnership with Dulux Fiji. Dulux Fiji will serve as the Official Paint Partner, with refurbishment expected to begin in the coming months.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI Rugby is set to restore pride in the home of the national game with a facelift for Rugby House and the High-Performance Unit (HPU) Gym through a new partnership with Dulux Fiji.

Dulux Fiji will serve as the Official Paint Partner, with refurbishment expected to begin in the coming months.

This project is more than a fresh coat of paint; it aims to improve Fiji Rugby’s working environment and strengthen the organisation’s foundations.

CEO Koli Sewabu said Rugby House must reflect the pride and professionalism of its staff and players.

“Every meaningful transformation begins with small but deliberate actions, and this is one of those moments,” Sewabu said.

“Rugby House is the heart of our organisation, and we want it to reflect the pride, professionalism and ambition of Fijian rugby.”

The refurbishment will upgrade facilities used daily by players, coaches, and staff preparing for national and international campaigns.

Sewabu emphasised that while on-field performance is important, behind-the-scenes work is equally crucial for Fiji Rugby’s long-term success.

He described the Dulux partnership as an investment in creating a more professional and inspiring environment.

Dulux Fiji CEO Roshan Singh said the company was honoured to support Fiji’s national sport, calling rugby a source of “pride, unity and inspiration” for the nation.

“We are honoured to play a small part in supporting Fiji Rugby by helping create spaces that reflect the pride and passion associated with our national sport.”

The refurbishment marks a key step in Fiji Rugby’s efforts to build a stronger organisation and renew Rugby House, the home of Fijian rugby.

item.title: A historic last four for Lomary
item.description: LOMARY Secondary School has qualified for the Under-18 Weet-Bix Raluve semi-finals for the first time in the school’s history following a 38-5 victory over Bua Central College last Saturday at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva. Assistant coach Samuela Gucake said the achievement was a significant milestone for the side, which had waited several years for an opportunity to reach the semifinals.
item.content:encoded:
LOMARY Secondary School has qualified for the Under-18 Weet-Bix Raluve semi-finals for the first time in the school’s history following a 38-5 victory over Bua Central College last Saturday at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

Assistant coach Samuela Gucake said the achievement was a significant milestone for the side, which had waited several years for an opportunity to reach the semifinals.

Gucake also acknowledged Bua Central, who travelled from Vanua Levu to compete in the competition.

“This is the first-time for us to be at the semifinal after so many years of competing in the girls’ division,” Gucake said.

He said the team would now focus on improving its execution ahead of next week’s semifinal, where the competition would become tougher.

“I believe we need to perfect our execution. We know that the competition will only get tougher.

Gucake said some players were playing rugby for the first time, making teamwork and preparation important heading into the semifinal.

He said the message to the players before the match was simple, give 100 per cent effort and have no excuses, regardless of the result.

Gucake thanked supporters who turned up for the match and called on more fans to support the team next week.

“We are calling on all the supporters next week to come out in numbers. Come in your blue colours and let’s support the girls,” he said.

item.title: Deans, Raluve semis set
item.description: FOUR Vodafone Super Deans and Weet-Bix Raluve semi-finals will be played alongside the Vodafone Fijiana XVs second Test match against South Africa in Churchill Park, Lautoka. The Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Interim committee, with the support of the Ministry of Education and Fiji Rakavi Football Union, has confirmed a two-venue program for the national semi-finals.
item.content:encoded:
FOUR Vodafone Super Deans and Weet-Bix Raluve semi-finals will be played alongside the Vodafone Fijiana XVs second Test match against South Africa in Churchill Park, Lautoka.

The Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Interim committee, with the support of the Ministry of Education and Fiji Rakavi Football Union, has confirmed a two-venue program for the national semi-finals.

The arrangement will give secondary school students the opportunity to play in front of a large crowd and share the stage with the Fijiana XV.

Interim committee representative Biu Colati said the program aimed at strengthening the development pathway for secondary schools rugby.

“Our priority has always been to provide the best possible experience for our student-athletes while continuing to strengthen the development pathway for secondary school rugby,” Colati said.

The Churchill Park program will begin with the Vodafone Super Deans under-14 semi-final between Ratu Navula College and Ratu Kadavulevu School, followed by the U19 clash between Ratu Navula College and Lelean Memorial School.

The Weet-Bix Raluve U16 semifinal between Sigatoka Methodist College and St Vincent College will also be played at Churchill Park.

The Fijiana XV will meet the Springbok women at 1pm in the second Test match, with Fiji aiming to level the series and retain the trophy.

The final school match of the day will be the Vodafone Super Deans U18 semi-final between Suva Grammar School and Ra High School. Ra has enjoyed a strong campaign after entering the Northern Division playoffs as the Western division’s fourth ranked qualifier. The remaining semi-finals will be played at the HFC Bank Stadium, Buckhurst ground 1 and Bidesi ground.

Confirmed semi-final fixtures for all grades; U14 – Ratu Navula College (RNC) v Ratu Kadavulevu School (west); Queen Victoria School (QVS) v Mahatma Ghandi Memorial (MGM) U15 – Lelean Memorial School (LMS) v Marist Brothers High School (MBHS); QVS v RKS; U16 – Nasinu Secondary School (NSS) v Suva Grammar School (SGS), QVS v MGM; U17 – Ba Methodist v RKS, QVS v SGS; U19 RNC v LMS(west); RKS v Navatu Secondary School; Raluve U16 – Sigatoka Methodist v St Vincent College (west); Adi Cakobau v NSS; Raluve U18 MGM v Adi Cakobau, Sila Central v Lomary Secondary; Deans U18 – SGS v Ra High (west), LMS v NSS
